objective.text: The investigation set out to measure and characterize the transient structure of diffusion flames established at initially non-steady, spherical flame structures.
objective.quote: Measure and characterize the transient structure (such as temperature and species distribution) of diffusion flames established at initially non-steady, spherical flame structures for mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios   (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty), for different flow rates.

fuel.text: Conventional gaseous fuels including hydrogen, methane, and ethylene were used.
fuel.quote: Conventional gaseous fuels including hydrogen, methane, and ethylene will be used.

sample_geometry.text: The experiments used a spherical porous burner to obtain a spherical flame.
sample_geometry.quote: issued into an oxidizing environment through a spherical porous burner and ignited to obtain, nominally, a spherical, one-dimensional stabilized flame.

variables.text: The tests varied mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios and different C2H4/diluent ratios for different flow rates.
variables.quote: mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios   (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty), for different flow rates.

measurements.text: Synchronized measurements included spectrally resolved images, flame and burner temperatures, and radiative flux measurements.
measurements.quote: Synchronized measurements are to be made including spectrally resolved images, flame and burner temperatures, radiative flux measurements, and system operating conditions

earth_benefits.text: Understanding diffusion flames improves combustion engine performance in terms of power, efficiency, pollutant emissions, and reliability.
earth_benefits.quote: understanding the underlying dynamics and chemistry of diffusion flames is important in improving performance in terms of power, efficiency, pollutant emissions, and reliability.
